unmapped_findings: The sample of interest, 12Al-10Mn-0.4C tempered at 600 °C, has no tabulated numeric property in the paper: Tables 2 (9Al-10Mn-1C), 4 (12Al-10Mn-1C), 5 (800 °C series), 8 (9Al-xMn-1C) and 9 (12Al-10Mn-1C and 9Al-10Mn-1C) do not list 12Al-10Mn-0.4C, so no Vickers hardness value could be assigned to this specific composition/condition.

The Fig. 3(a) caption writes '2Al-10Mn-0.4C' while the citing text refers to the same 600 °C-tempered alloy as '12Al-10Mn-0.4C'; this discrepancy is reflected in the sample aliases, and Fig. 3(a) is treated here as the 12Al-10Mn-0.4C 600 °C condition.

The 'slight hardening effects (Table 4)' and 'generic precipitation transformation' discussion (b0037) is explicitly tied to Fig. 4 and Table 4, which are captioned/entitled for 12Al-10Mn-1C, not for 12Al-10Mn-0.4C; therefore those hardening numbers were NOT assigned to this sample.

The single supplied Fig. 3 panel shows a strongly banded, lamellar microstructure, but the figure description states it cannot be assigned between (a) 2Al/12Al-10Mn-0.4C and (b) 12Al-10Mn-1C from the pixels alone; it is therefore not used as a confirmed micrograph of this sample.

The passage tying 'an austenite matrix only featured by carbon-depleted γ regions with globular κ-carbides' to the 12% Al transformation (b0035) and the figure description both attribute that morphology to the 12Al-10Mn-1C (Fig. 3(b)) case; for 12Al-10Mn-0.4C the text only states that precipitation produced a 'multifaceted microstructure' with reactions involving the whole γ volume.

The CALPHAD phase-fraction diagrams (Fig. 9) cover 9Al-10Mn-0.4 and 9Al-10Mn-1C and those in Fig. 12 cover 9Al-20Mn-1C, 9Al-30Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C and 12Al-30Mn-1C; no computed phase-fraction diagram is presented for 12Al-10Mn-0.4C, so no computational data are attached to this sample.
